pr_title: gh-102515: Remove unused imports in the `Lib/` directory
pr_body:
Identified using the `pycln` tool; manually reviewed by me.

<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-102515 -->
* Fixes gh-102515
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->
pr_comments: Maybe worth commenting some of the less-obvious, required imports for next time?
Of the 34 files with 'extra' imports, 28 are in test.  If the tests pass, we may assume that the deletions are really unused.  I am checking the deletions in regular code and already found an error.
Guido refuted my comment about not checking tests, and found the issue with multliprocessing.connection.  I consider that to be a bug in pycln.

> I consider that to be a bug in pycln.

It's an imperfect tool, and the stdlib is possibly the worst kind of code to judge it on. I've had good experiences with using the tool on other projects, but if you simply run `pycln Lib --all` in the CPython repo, it removes 290 imports from 150 files. Most of these are false positives.
Thanks @gvanrossum, @terryjreedy and @kumaraditya303 for the careful reviews! Much appreciated.

issue_context.title: Unused imports in the `Lib/` directory
issue_context.body:
The [`pycln`](https://github.com/hadialqattan/pycln) tool has highlighted 34 files in the `Lib/` directory which appear to have unnecessary imports.

<!-- gh-linked-prs -->
### Linked PRs
* gh-102516
<!-- /gh-linked-prs -->

review_comments: This one is actually necessary. It is later relied on when `mp.connection.wait` is called on L407. Without this import we are not guaranteed that `import multiprocessing as mp` causes `mp.connection` to exist.
Good catch. It concerns me that no tests appeared to fail when this import was removed.
Oh, I suppose `multiprocessing.connection` was still imported and stored as `mp.connection` through some side effect somewhere...

Yeah, and when that code gets changed this might break. Maybe add a comment? (This is the kind of thing that pyright is very picky about, and in this case I agree -- we were bitten by this kind of bug at Dropbox numerous times.)
A comment might be more helpful than using an odd idiom to please a tool.

For the record, I pushed the change because I personally find it easier to understand the code if the import is more explicit, not to please a tool :)

But happy to revert the commit, and add a comment instead!
Looks like this is used by various strings (templates) that are run via `self.run_test()`.
Interesting, no tests appear to fail if this import is removed. (I checked.)
Oh, you're right. The template also imports this, L40. Nvm then.
Could this one possibly be here intentionally for some side effect? @kumaraditya303
Still waiting for @kumaraditya303 to wake up. :-)
No it can be removed. Only `asyncio.events` has side effect of registering fork handler and that too is already imported by `asyncio` so no worries.
